lesson.title: Project clinic: reproducible artifacts and defensible conclusions
lesson.short: Environment · data lineage · smoke tests · report assembly
lesson.timeMeaning: Suggested independent study minutes; not scheduled contact time
lesson.lead: A useful artifact lets another person trace a figure back to inputs, code, settings and raw measurements.
goals: Package the evidence required to rerun a result.
Separate a smoke test from a full scientific reproduction.
Audit cost, data permission, limitations and claims before presenting.

sections.title: Start here: prerequisites and course status
sections.html:
A teammate has the code but cannot rebuild your chart. Which missing link stops them: input, configuration, timing protocol or raw output? This lesson assembles the chain and budgets the work before a full run.

Bring your frozen question, protocol and claim from lessons 32–34. All manifests and budget figures are original suggestions, not course submission requirements. This supplemental clinic is not an Edinburgh lecture or verified Canvas assignment; the instructor's real rules, deadlines and submission route remain unverified.

sections.title: Define the artifact boundary
sections.html:
Start at the figure and walk backward: plotted value → raw results → command/configuration → code and dependencies → input identity → environment. A repository link covers only part of this chain. Someone following it must be able to see what produced the claimed observation.

Record hardware model/count, memory, driver/runtime, interconnect, CPU/RAM/storage, operating system and concurrency limits. A container preserves much software state, but not identical hardware, external services, data or all numerical behavior.

For inputs, record provenance, version, preprocessing and license. If full data cannot be shared, provide a small public or synthetic check and say which results cannot be independently rerun. Do not redistribute restricted files or credentials. Artifact-evaluation guidance offers useful distinctions between an artifact that runs and evidence that results reproduce; this companion grants no badge or course status.

Key takeaway

Reproducibility is a traceable chain of evidence, not just a link to code.

Sources for this section: ACM SIGSIM PADS 2024: Reproducibility and Artifact Evaluation. Numerical traces marked original are teaching examples, not reported measurements.

sections.title: Worked example: a minimal run manifest
sections.html:
Construct one original run manifest as a chain of answers. Identity: experiment ID, commit, configuration hash, timestamp and responsible member. Inputs: dataset version/hash, query split, model/embedding/prompt revision and seed. Environment: package lock, runtime, hardware, resource limits and background load.

Protocol: warm-up, repetitions, trial order, timing boundary, timeout and quality target. Outputs: raw-result path, error logs, correctness result, figure and generation command. Cost: CPU/device elapsed use, service calls, peak memory and any price assumptions. A checksum detects changed bytes; it does not prove correct data.

The README says “run latest on the standard dataset.” What prevents a rerun?

Both names can change. Specify exact code/dependencies, data/preprocessing, command/configuration, environment and protocol, then connect raw outputs to the figure. Keep secrets out of version control and inspect logs for sensitive query or document text before sharing.

sections.title: A two-level execution path
sections.html:
Offer two execution paths. The smoke test uses tiny public/synthetic input, runs quickly and checks installation, schema, expected results and output paths. If that fails, debugging is cheap. Label it clearly: it does not reproduce paper-scale performance.

The full path lists actual preparation, resource/time needs, evaluation command, raw-output format and figure command. Include restart/retry behavior and explicit expensive API or disk requirements; a setup script must not silently launch paid cloud work.

Ask a teammate to follow instructions in a clean allowed environment. Record changed defaults, missing paths, unavailable dependencies and nondeterminism. If the chart changes, investigate the chain instead of copying the old chart.

The smoke test matches expected output. Is the benchmark reproduced?

No. The small case validates the basic path. Performance reproduction requires the declared scale, environment, protocol and comparison, with differences reported. It is useful to know exactly which level passed.

sections.title: Budget the experiment rather than only the final run
sections.html:
Budget every repeated operation. One query repetition takes one GPU for six minutes. Twenty configurations × five repetitions × six minutes =600 GPU-minutes=10 GPU-hours. Data preparation is one CPU-hour once; keep that resource separate.

If each configuration's index build takes four GPU-minutes and is reused, builds add 20×4=80 GPU-minutes. Total=680 GPU-minutes=11⅓ GPU-hours. Rebuilding before every repetition instead adds 20×5×4=400; total=1,000 GPU-minutes=16⅔ GPU-hours. Builds can be outside query timing while remaining inside the experiment budget.

GPU-hours are not wall time when work overlaps or uses multiple devices. CPU-hours cannot simply be added as GPU-hours. Include failed runs, profiling, tuning and artifact checks. For one/two H100s, inspect memory headroom before allocating. Plan a small pilot and an explicit budget stop; one successful run cannot answer variability.

Why state whether builds are reused?

The query comparison might be unchanged, but the total resource estimate differs by 320 GPU-minutes. A reader deciding feasibility needs the reuse rule, not just the final search time.

sections.title: Assemble a report that does not overclaim
sections.html:
Build the report around one question and the evidence answering it: motivation, related work, design/assumptions, methodology, results, ablations, limitations and artifact path. Put each claim next to its supporting figure, with units, sample count and quality target visible.

Maintain a claim-evidence ledger. For “scales better,” identify the scaling axis, fixed resources, workload, uncertainty and figure. Separate measured results, theoretical guarantees, analytical estimates and future work. Hypothetical illustration is not measured evidence.

You computed memory from vector dimensions but did not instrument allocations. How should it appear?

As an analytical estimate, with workspace and other omissions listed. It is not measured peak memory. If fitting memory is central to the claim, measure it before concluding feasibility.

Make sure each member can explain the central result and one failure. Assemble actual required deliverables only from the instructor's confirmed instructions.

Key takeaway

State what ran, what was measured and what remains an inference.

questions.question: Does a container alone guarantee bit-identical scientific reproduction?
options: No; hardware, data, external services and numerical/runtime behavior also matter.
Yes, regardless of hardware or input data.
Yes, if the image is large enough.
No, so containers have no value.
questions.explanation: Containers preserve part of the software environment. Reproducibility still depends on the complete evidence and execution boundary.

options: The paper-scale performance result is reproduced.
The basic execution path works on that test input.
Every dataset license permits redistribution.
The main hypothesis is universally true.
questions.explanation: A smoke test checks setup and a small functional path, not the full scientific claim.

questions.question: A run uses 6 GPU-minutes; there are 20 configurations and 5 repetitions. What is the total query-run budget, excluding preparation/build costs?
options: 30 GPU-minutes
120 GPU-minutes
600 GPU-minutes
6,000 GPU-minutes
questions.explanation: There are 20×5=100 query repetitions. At 6 GPU-minutes each, the query budget is 600 GPU-minutes=10 GPU-hours. Data preparation and index builds are excluded here and must be added under their stated reuse rule. GPU-hours are resource usage, not necessarily elapsed wall time.

questions.question: What should happen to API keys before sharing an artifact?
options: Remove them from code/logs and document approved credential setup without exposing secrets.
Put them in the figure caption.
Encode them in base64.
Include them so reviewers can run immediately.
questions.explanation: Encoding is not protection. Shared artifacts and logs must not expose credentials or unauthorized data.
